children: CIBC Capital Economics chief economist Avery Shenfeld leans toward a Bank of Canada rate hike on Wednesday, even though tame core inflation and heightened trade uncertainty would justify a hold. Shenfeld says Governor Tiff Macklem's relatively hawkish remarks about a possible rate hike is the deciding factor behind his call. In the event of a hike, the BOC likely justifies the move "by citing the risk that persistent pressure on fuel costs and other upstream [fuel] prices will filter into broader CPI measures," Shenfeld tells WSJ. Macklem will also likely play down the risks to GDP growth posed by elevated US-Canada trade tensions, he adds. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)
